commits.title: Add performance guidance to get_available_variations() docblock (#62715)
Replace get_available_variations() with get_visible_children() in product-image.php (#62754)
Use variation objects instead of arrays in ProductPrice block (#62797)
VariationSelectorAttribute: Use variation objects instead of arrays for better performance (#62795)
Product Gallery: Use variation objects instead of arrays for better performance (#62792)
Performance: Store tax display option in variation price loop (#61782)

clusters.measured_connection: The report's variable-product lane and PRs #23-#25 sit in the same area: avoid full per-variation payload generation, title sync, term lookups, repeated parent-level price work, and repeated tax-display option reads inside variation price loops. The gateway deep dive adds a new overlay: WooPayments multicurrency hooks still run roughly 40k times on the same 800-variation page.
clusters.handoff: Keep replacing broad get_available_variations array hydration with narrower child/object paths where possible. For unavoidable full payloads, cache taxonomy labels, parent price-range decisions, tax display state, and gateway price/currency state per request.

clusters.cluster: Product object caching and product-loop cache priming

commits.title: Wooplug 5884/product object cache (#62041)
Change Cache Product Objects default plugin compatibility to COMPATIBLE (#63243)
Enable product object caching by default for new installs (#65445)
Performance: Add cache priming for grouped product child product loops (#61784)

clusters.measured_connection: The heavy order edit and checkout lanes still show repeated object/meta hydration. PR #28 applies the same cache-priming idea to order item meta for single-order admin loads.
clusters.handoff: Look for remaining places that instantiate many product/order/item objects without first priming the matching raw meta and object caches.

clusters.cluster: HPOS caching, search, and status filtering

commits.title: Move HPOS Datastore caching out of experimental features. (#61521)
Fix HPOS to exclude internal statuses when status='any' (#61856)
Exclude checkout-draft orders from default REST API order queries (#63743)
Add OrderUtil::custom_orders_table_data_sync_is_enabled() accessor (#65649)

clusters.measured_connection: The HPOS admin search/count lane and gateway settings pages both show HPOS order-count/search overhead. The gateway deep dive also shows repeated DataSynchronizer option reads for woocommerce_custom_orders_table_background_sync_mode.
clusters.handoff: Continue reducing repeated HPOS datastore setup and broad counts/searches. Cache request-local DataSynchronizer state and avoid broad admin counts when a page does not need them synchronously.

commits.title: Performance: Strip the rel=self link from the report response as it is built by the Reports/Controller (#60791)
Performance improvements to analytics reports endpoints. (#61263)
Update WooCommerce Analytics REST API Namespaces to lazy load for improved performance. (#60684)

clusters.measured_connection: The pathological and CRUD-invariant reports still show broad revenue/product stats aggregates as an open lane. These commits reduce API boot and report response overhead but do not remove the large aggregate SQL shapes.
clusters.handoff: Separate REST namespace boot cost from report datastore aggregate cost. The remaining hard work is precomputation/index-windowing for wc_order_stats and wc_order_product_lookup aggregates.

commits.title: Introduce read multiple to shipping zones (#60917)

clusters.measured_connection: This commit improves reading multiple known shipping zones by adding WC_Shipping_Zones::get_shipping_zones() and data-store read_multiple(). The measured shipping/tax lane is one step earlier: get_zone_id_from_package() still loads all postcode locations before it knows the candidate zone IDs.
clusters.handoff: A shipping postcode fix should feed a short candidate zone list into the existing bulk-read capable path, using persisted normalized exact/wildcard/range candidate data rather than loading every postcode location first.

clusters.cluster: Blocks frontend enqueue and resource-hint overhead

commits.title: Improve the performance of Blocks\AssetsController::get_block_asset_resource_hints() (#61015)
Improve performance when enqueueing block styles for classic themes (#60990)

clusters.measured_connection: These commits were not the dominant backend SQL/function lanes in the current request profiles, but they are relevant to frontend product/category requests where WooCommerce Blocks assets are booted under classic themes or resource hints are generated.
clusters.handoff: Add a targeted frontend follow-up with classic-theme product archive, product page, cart, and checkout requests. Profile block asset enqueue/resource-hint call counts separately from product query, variation payload, and gateway price hooks.

clusters.cluster: Store API, sessions, and feature boot guardrails

commits.title: Reject non-WC_Order objects in Store API order authorization (#64568)
Make abandoned cart recovery experimental and opt-in (not default-on for new installs) (#65521)
Add experimental feature to destroy empty WooCommerce sessions (#60855)
Add default_plugin_compatibility option to Session Destroying (#61177)

clusters.measured_connection: The cart/checkout and Store API-adjacent lanes measured in this report still spend most time in tax/shipping SQL, gateway hooks, and queue/order-item work. A targeted Store API session probe now shows the guardrail detail: fresh empty carts do not create a session row, every valid Cart-Token read performs one direct wp_woocommerce_sessions SELECT via StoreApi\SessionHandler, and remove-item can leave a residual empty-cart session row containing shipping/gateway/removed-cart keys.
clusters.handoff: Keep this separated from the high-confidence backend fixes. If optimizing the session lane, define a Store API-safe cleanup policy for residual keys after carts become empty, and consider whether tokenized Store API reads should share a short request/object-cache layer for absent or unchanged session rows. Do not blindly apply regular cookie-session destroy-empty-sessions behavior to Cart-Token sessions without extension compatibility checks.

commits.title: Wooplug 5655/defer term counting for batch product editing (#61383)
Only update term counts when product visibility changes (#61457)
Skip category processing in product permalinks when not needed (#63121)
Cache Store API products last modified timestamp (#63228)

clusters.measured_connection: The Store API product collection-data and catalog paths still have broad count/query costs. These commits reduce surrounding product-list churn, but the remaining measured costs are query-shape and count aggregation problems.
clusters.handoff: Keep shrinking product-list per-item work, but prioritize Store API count SQL and unbounded ID materialization for the largest residual wins.

interpretation: The author history points to the same architectural themes seen in profiling: avoid full variation payloads, prime/cache object data before loops, reduce HPOS broad counts/searches, lazy-load analytics/report code, make shipping-zone data access bulk-aware, trim frontend Blocks boot overhead, and keep costly features opt-in. The remaining measured bottlenecks are generally the next layer down: broad SQL candidate selection, unbounded aggregate/count queries, queue claiming over large pending-action tables, gateway remote calls during render, and per-item meta persistence.
